notes: RBox revision of a role chain: stands_in ∘ in_time_zone ⊑ in_time_zone (a building keeps the time zone of the city it stands in) is removed. Replaces the earlier drainage-basin chain (in_drainage_basin_of ∘ drains_into), which the models do not hold: its direct question was missed by 2 of 4, the Spanish instance by all 4 and the Chinese by 3 (Rule 6), and reviewers flagged that Vienna and Lyon draining to the Black Sea and the Mediterranean are stored facts. Every model holds the time-zone chain (the README's own example of a derived fact, the Space Needle's time zone), and a building's time zone is almost never written down, so the instances cannot be answered from a stored sentence about the building and turn on the chain. New relation stands_in (building or landmark in a city) in staging/geography-replace-rbox.RELATIONS.md, tagged with this chain only; no other tag gives a building a time zone, so there is no premise route back to the old chain. The statement is written positively ("can observe a different time zone") so the negation question has a single negation. Yes and no: the first instance (and the cross-lingual queries) asks whether the time zone follows (yes, then no), the second whether, given only the facts, the Alamo could keep another time zone (no, then yes). Brussels and the Atomium avoid the Brandenburg Gate and the Gateway Arch, which other geography records use. The Rhine side fact (missed by 2) is replaced by Mount Everest. Near asks another role chain in the topic (capital_of, chain:located_in->located_in), reference yes, differing from the new no. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
